data.title: Oppenheimer Holdings Shares Fall on Lower 3Q Profit, Revenue
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Shares of Oppenheimer Holdings lost more than a fifth of their value after the company posted lower profit and revenue in the third quarter, citing lower retail trading and a decline in investment banking volume.

Shares of Oppenheimer were down 20%, or at $86.20, through market-close on Friday. The stock is up 19% year to date.

The investment bank and broker-dealer posted a third-quarter profit of $5.5 million, or 47 cents a share, compared with $21.7 million, or $1.90 the year before. The readout was impacted by a $21 million pre-tax expense associated with a long-term employee incentive compensation program for financial advisors tied to the company's stock.

On an adjusted basis, per-share earnings were $1.81 cents, compared with $2.77 the year before.

Revenue fell 10% to $382 million from $424.4 million.

Chief Executive Robert Lowenthal said earnings were lower due to lower retail trading activity, reduced investment banking volumes and a higher expense associated with the increased value of stock appreciation rights.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com.

data.title: Intel, Amazon, Nvidia, ExxonMobil, Sandisk, FedEx Freight, and More Stocks That Explain Today's Market — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Adam Clark, Mariapaula Gonzalez, and Kit Norton

Stocks fell Friday and extended the previous session's declines after a slew of disappointing earnings from big technology companies rattled investors and led to a tech selloff.

Intel plunged 29% and was the worst performer in the S&P 500 for the trading session. Its underwhelming guidance surprised investors, following a fatal explosion at one of its facilities. The company's weak forecast for the personal-computer market also dragged down peers Dell Technologies and HP Inc., which declined 11% and 8.7%, respectively.

Amazon.com fell 2% after third-quarter earnings came in below Wall Street's expectations on the back of revenue from retail and advertising.

Sandisk dropped 12%. The semiconductor reported fiscal first-quarter revenue and profit that beat Wall Street's estimates. Its board of directors also approved an 8-for-1 stock split, with split-adjusted trading expected to start Nov. 30.

Nvidia fell 4.2% following other chip makers lower as the wider tech sector sold off. The stock was on pace to close out October with a decline of more than 10% which would mark the stock's worst monthly performance since November 2025, when it fell 12.6%, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

The tech selloff also was taking down cloud-computing companies. CoreWeave and Nebius Group declined 10% and 8.8%, respectively. Chip stocks were also falling with Advanced Micro Devices falling 11%.

Reddit was among the worst performers in the S&P 500, plummeting 29%. The company's third-quarter earnings showed weaker-than-expected user growth as traffic trends continue to face pressures from Google search updates.

Alphabet declined 1.1% after logging its worst every daily percentage decline on Wednesday of 12.6% as the company's core advertising business in search and YouTube struggled.

Cryptocurrency stocks slumped as the digital asset space was hit with a $6.3 billion hack at Binance, the largest crypto exchange. Coinbase Global fell 13%, Robinhood Markets dropped 8.6%, and Circle Internet declined 9%.

Twilio sank 17% after lowering its revenue guidance for the fourth quarter, raising concerns that its AI business hasn't been living up to expectations.

Roblox dropped 21%. The gaming company said the number of daily active users on its platform dropped 9% from a year ago to 138 million during the third quarter, while engagement hours fell 15% to 34 billion.

Alphatec plunged 38% after missing third-quarter estimates and slashing its full-year revenue guidance. The stock was on pace for its worst daily percentage decline since August 2015, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

Illumina declined 18%. Though the company raised its fiscal-year outlook and beat earnings estimates, it wasn't enough to escape the broader technology selloff.

Things were brighter for oil companies. ExxonMobil and Chevron each gained about 1.3% after the two supermajors both banked huge third-quarter profits.

The best-performing stock on Friday in the S&P 500, meanwhile, was FedEx Freight, which advanced 15%. Management raised its outlook for adjusted operating profit for the transition period from June 1 through Dec. 31, to $695 million to $715 million, up from a prior guidance of $605 million to $645 million. Shares of FedEx gained 3.2%.

Write to Adam Clark at adam.clark@barrons.com, Mariapaula Gonzalez at mariapaula.gonzalez@barrons.com and Kit Norton at kit.norton@barrons.com

data.title: Standex International Posts Record Q1 Sales of $232.6 Million, Raises FY27 Outlook
data.description:
Standex International reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 sales of $232.6 million, up 7.0% year over year, with organic growth of 12.4%. GAAP operating income was $40.4 million and net income from continuing operations was $24.2 million; adjusted diluted EPS rose 21.1% to $2.41. The company raised its fiscal 2027 outlook, citing expanding backlog and multiple growth drivers.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue: Net sales were $232.6 million, compared with $217.4 million a year earlier.
  • Gross profit: $103.2 million; GAAP gross margin was 44.4%, a record, and adjusted gross margin was also a record 44.4%, up 240 basis points year over year.
  • Operating income: GAAP operating income was $40.4 million, versus $29.6 million; adjusted operating income was $47.0 million, up 13.1%. GAAP operating margin was 17.4% and adjusted operating margin was 20.2%.
  • Net income: Net income from continuing operations was $24.2 million, compared with $15.8 million. Adjusted net income from continuing operations was $29.3 million, up 21.8%.
  • Adjusted diluted EPS: $2.41, up 21.1% from $1.99. GAAP diluted EPS was $1.99.

Business Highlights

  • Electronics led segment performance, with organic growth of 29.5% and a book-to-bill ratio of 1.23. The segment recorded approximately $173 million in orders.
  • Order intake reached a company record of approximately $273 million, with a total-company book-to-bill ratio of 1.17.
  • Sales into fast-growth markets were approximately $78 million. The company expects those markets to grow more than 20% year over year to over $315 million in fiscal 2027.
  • Standex expects to release more than 20 new products in fiscal 2027, which it anticipates will contribute more than 300 basis points of incremental growth.
  • Demand supported by electrification, data centers, defense, and a recovery in general industrial markets contributed to growth. Engraving & Hydraulics faced softness in North American automotive markets.

data.title: AMD's stock slides after Intel earnings reveal two big issues
data.description:
By Emily Bary and Hannah Pedone

Intel is struggling to make enough AI server chips and dealing with a weak PC market. Investors will soon find out the degree to which AMD may be suffering from the same problems.

AMD reports earnings on Tuesday and will offer its own read on the PC and server markets.

Advanced Micro Devices shares are getting caught up in the intense market reaction to Intel's earnings.

Intel (INTC) is experiencing twin pressures within its business. Sales of personal computers are weakening due to inflated memory-chip prices, and the company isn't able to make enough server chips to satisfy robust demand for central processing units.

Since AMD (AMD), like Intel, makes CPUs for both PCs and data centers, the question for AMD investors concerns the degree to which Intel's issues are related to industrywide dynamics versus company-specific missteps.

Shares of AMD closed down 11% on Friday, while Intel's stock closed down 29%.

AMD is due to post its own earnings on Tuesday afternoon.

The troubles in the PC market likely extend beyond Intel. Even before Intel's report, third-party estimates indicated industrywide PC shipments were down by some 20% in the third quarter relative to the same period a year earlier. That marked an escalation from the mid-single-digit decline seen in the second quarter, Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon wrote in a preview of both AMD's and Intel's earnings.

Following Intel's report, Cantor Fitzgerald analyst C.J. Muse wrote that a "decline in the PC market is not a surprise," given high memory prices, but the extent of Intel's declines proved "a meaningful surprise." The company's results implied a 45% drop in unit sales relative to a year earlier, he said.

The "gloomy comments on the PC market for the rest of 2026 and 2027 will likely weigh on any company with PC exposure, such as AMD," Morningstar analyst Brian Colello told MarketWatch.

Intel's management team noted that while elevated memory prices are crimping PC demand, another issue is that corporate information-technology teams now face more limited budgets for equipment purchases.

That said, PCs are a bigger deal for Intel than they are for AMD. StoneX analyst Cody Acree told MarketWatch that AMD could generate less than a quarter of its sales this year from PCs, while Intel's client group, which includes PC chips, is expected to account for more than half of revenue.

That means Intel is "much more exposed, but AMD is exposed none the less," he said.

Meanwhile, some of Intel's problems in server chips might relate to its own poor execution. In particular, the company seems to have misjudged the respective demand outlooks for the PC and server businesses, leaving it with too much production capacity for PC chips, all while it can't meet the booming server demand.

Chip companies across the board can't satisfy all the demand for artificial-intelligence chips, but the issues might be especially pronounced at Intel. Cantor Fitzgerald's Muse noted Intel's "clear loss of share to AMD in servers."

Another thing AMD has working in its favor, according to BofA analyst Vivek Arya, is that the company also sells graphics processing units for AI. The ramp of its Helios rack-scale offering could be a "strong positive offset," he noted.

StoneX's Acree said in a note to clients that "Intel's PC warning, and the likely AMD stock pressure, could lower expectations before Tuesday, creating room for AMD's smaller client exposure and data-center ramp to produce a better relative outcome."

-Emily Bary -Hannah Pedone

data.title: US bonds rally, sending yields to biggest monthly decline since 2023
data.description:
Key points:
  • Intel and Amazon weigh on stocks
  • 10-year yield has biggest monthly fall since 2023
  • Nasdaq ends more than 2% lower

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Harry Robertson

US Treasuries rose on Friday, and the benchmark 10-year yield closed the month with its biggest monthly drop in nearly three years, as a sharp selloff in technology-related stocks pushed investors into the safe-haven asset.

The yield on the 10-year US Treasury was last down 36 basis points for October, most for a month since December 2023. It also had a fourth straight week of declines, its longest such stretch in a year.

The Nasdaq fell more than 2% after earnings reports from Amazon and Intel rattled investors already concerned about the rising costs of the AI buildout.

The rally in US Treasuries prices in recent weeks follows a sharp selloff that pushed yields to multi-decade highs on worries about rising energy costs and rising government debt.

"The last few weeks have just been an absolute sentiment shift," said Gennadiy Goldberg, head of US rates strategy at TD Securities in New York. "The risks have really started to re-emerge, whereas a few weeks prior to that, everything was viewed as an upside risk to rates."

"To some extent, for rates investors, this is a question of whether the AI jitters persist or whether this is just a bump in the road on the way to rates remaining higher for longer."

Expectations for a December US interest rate hike remain high after the Federal Reserve this week left rates unchanged and upgraded its assessment of the economy. Rate futures are pricing in about a 70% chance of a quarter-point hike from the Fed in December, according to the CME FedWatch tool on Friday. That is down from about 78% late Thursday.

Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said on Friday the US central bank needs to raise rates at least two more times to get inflation under control.

The Fed in September raised rates for the first time in three years in an effort to combat higher inflation, tied in part to high energy prices and the AI boom.

"It's not like we think that this should be interpreted as a dovish shift," said JoAnne Bianco, partner and senior investment strategist at BondBloxx Investment Management. "We think the committee still remains prepared to tighten further if necessary. A December hike is very much on the table."

The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was last down 6.4 bps at 4.925%, and earlier hit its lowest level since mid-September. The yield on the 30-year bond (US30YT=RR) was down 1.9 bps at 5.31%, and was also set for its biggest monthly drop since December 2023.

The two-year (US2YT=RR) US Treasury yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, was down 8.1 bps at 4.575%. It was set for its biggest monthly fall since August 2025.

AMAZON AND INTEL SHARES BOTH FALL

Amazon's shares fell after the company reported a sharp cash outflow and another increase in spending, while chipmaker Intel was down 29% after it warned that it would burn cash this year. Yields also fell on Thursday after disappointing results from top AI player Alphabet .

The Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge - climbed 0.5% last month, in line with expectations, while the US economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter.

A closely watched part of the US Treasury yield curve measuring the gap between yields on two- and 10-year Treasury notes (US2US10=TWEB), seen as an indicator of economic expectations, was at 34.6 bps.

The breakeven rate on five-year US Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) (US5YTIP=TWEB) was last at 2.461% after closing at 2.469% on Thursday.

The 10-year TIPS breakeven rate (US10YTIP=TWEB) was last at 2.336%, indicating the market sees inflation averaging about 2.3% a year for the next decade.
